Q: Implementing plugin architecture pattern in .NET MAUI Blazor Hybrid A:

How do you see Apple and Google allowing you to load and execute arbitrary code on their platforms? You compare it to something that is borderline insecure, starting from taking over as admin, going through unauthorized file uploads, and finishing with executing code remotely.

Also, my opinion, even if this was possible: this "pattern", for me is "anti-pattern". If it is done precisely, with strict contract between the host and the plugins? Okay. But implementing it on your own? When the example code looks like this: Activator.CreateInstance(type)?

Q: DO-WHILE loop challenge A:

Inside the do block, after reading the user input, add an if block that also check for the password, and decrement the maxAttempts as needed. Now the condition for while should also check that maxAttempts is not yet 0. You also shouldn't automatically declare the password is correct after exiting the do-while block, move that inside an if block that only run if maxAttempts is still larger than 0.

Q: How to compress images and save quality using PHP A:

If you want to compress images in the browser without uploading them to a server, you can do it entirely client-side using WebAssembly.

This approach has a few advantages:

  • No upload → better privacy
  • Faster (no network round trip)
  • No server cost

A typical implementation uses:

  • Canvas for preprocessing
  • WebAssembly codecs (e.g. mozjpeg / oxipng / webp)

For example, modern tools run compression fully in-browser using WASM, which allows near-native performance compared to JavaScript solutions :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}.

If you don’t want to build everything yourself, I built a small tool that does this: https://picbind.com

It supports batch compression and runs entirely locally in your browser.

Q: Make git undo any whitespace-only changes? A:

If your changes are not staged

To stage changes that are not just whitespace changes, you can do:

git diff -U0 -w --no-color |
  git apply --cached --ignore-whitespace --unidiff-zero -

Afterwards, to remove all unstaged changes (those changes that differ only in whitespace), you can do:

git checkout . (or, in newer gits, git restore .)

If your changes are staged

Unstage your changes by doing a git reset --mixed and continue from the top of this answer. Note that mixed is the default mode and can be omitted.
